stem: Evolution means ____.
solution: **(B)** Gradual change. Evolution is the gradual change occurring in living organisms over a long duration. New organs do not appear suddenly; existing organs change slowly over thousands of years, so a quick change is not evolution.

stem: One of the rare species is ____.
solution: **(B)** Red panda. Rare species are those whose numbers have declined considerably and which, being endemic, may become extinct very fast; the red panda and the musk deer are examples. The lesser florican is an endangered species and the tiger is a vulnerable species.

stem: The machine which converts the kinetic energy of wind to electrical energy is called ____.
solution: **(D)** Wind turbine. In a wind turbine the kinetic energy of the blowing wind rotates the blades, and the rotation drives a generator that produces electrical energy. A solar cell converts light energy, not wind energy, into electricity.

stem: Chemically, vinegar is ____.
solution: **(A)** Acetic acid. Chemically, vinegar is about 4% acetic acid \(\left(CH_3COOH\right)\). It is produced from alcohol by acetic acid bacteria and is used to give a sour taste to food.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: We get ____ kcal energy per gram of proteins.
solution: **(A)** 4. We get 4 kcal of energy per gram of proteins, the same as per gram of carbohydrates. Lipids give more, 9 kcal per gram.

stem: Find odd man out: Starfish, Snail, Frog, Amoeba
solution: Frog is the odd one out. Frog is a chordate (class Amphibia), whereas starfish (Echinodermata), snail (Mollusca) and amoeba (Protozoa) are all non-chordates.

stem: Match the correct pairs: Column 'A': (1) Biotic components ; Column 'B': (a) Soil, (b) Plant, (c) Sunlight.
solution: Biotic components : (b) Plant. Biotic components are the living factors of the environment, such as plants and animals. Soil and sunlight are abiotic (non-living) components.

stem: Write the correlation: White revolution : Dairy :: Blue revolution : ____
solution: Blue revolution : Fisheries (production of fish and other useful aquatic organisms). White revolution increased milk production through dairy, and blue revolution is the production of various useful aquatic organisms such as fishes and shrimps with the help of water (pisciculture).

stem: Observe the diagram and identify the phylum:
solution: The diagram shows Hydra (with a bud), which belongs to phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria). Its cylindrical (polyp) body is radially symmetrical and diploblastic, with cnidoblast-bearing tentacles around the mouth.

stem: State, whether given statement is right or wrong: Peer group influence is stronger in case of adolescents.
solution: Right. Adolescents prefer the company of friends and follow their good or bad habits instead of the advice of parents and teachers, so peer-group influence is stronger in their case.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Give scientific reason: Fibers are one of the important nutrients.
solution: We cannot digest fibers, but they help in the digestion of other food substances and in the egestion of undigested substances from the body. They therefore keep the digestive system working properly and prevent constipation. Fibers are obtained from leafy vegetables, fruits and cereals. Hence fibers are considered one of the important (essential) nutrients.

stem: Give scientific reason: Though tortoise lives on land as well as in water, it cannot be included in class-Amphibia.
solution: Amphibians are strictly aquatic during larval life, have moist skin without any derivatives (used for respiration), have no neck and have digits without claws. A tortoise has none of these features: its body is covered by a dry, hard scaly shell, it breathes only through lungs, it has a neck, its digits bear claws and it has no aquatic larval stage. These are characters of class Reptilia. Hence, though it lives on land as well as in water, a tortoise is a reptile and cannot be included in class Amphibia.

stem: Give scientific reason: Hydroelectric energy, solar energy and wind energy are called renewable energies.
solution: Flowing water, sunlight and wind are sources that are replenished continuously by nature. Using them to produce electricity does not use them up, so they will not get exhausted, unlike coal, petroleum and natural gas whose reserves are limited. They also do not cause air pollution. Hence hydroelectric, solar and wind energy are called renewable energies.

stem: Write down four benefits of Biotechnology.
solution: Benefits of biotechnology: (1) It has become possible to increase the per hectare yield of crops irrespective of the limitations of crop-land area. (2) Expenses on disease control have been minimised since disease-resistant varieties were developed. (3) Fast fruit-setting varieties have increased the yield per annum. (4) Stress-resistant varieties that withstand variable temperature, water stress and changing soil fertility have been developed.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Distinguish between Sexual reproduction and Asexual reproduction.
solution:
| Sexual reproduction | Asexual reproduction |
|---|---|
| It occurs with the help of two germ cells (male and female gametes). | It occurs with the help of somatic cells, without gametes. |
| Male and female parents are necessary (biparental). | Only one parent is involved (uniparental). |
| Gametes are formed by meiosis and the zygote divides by mitosis. | It occurs by mitosis only. |
| Fertilisation takes place, and the offspring show variation due to genetic recombination. | There is no fertilisation; the offspring are genetically identical to the parent. |

stem: Write down any two features of Industrial Microbiology.
solution: Industrial microbiology is the commercial use of microbes in economic, social and environment-related processes and products. Its main features: (1) Various products are made with the help of the fermentation process, for example bread, cheese, wine, raw material for chemicals, enzymes, nutrients and medicines. (2) Microbes are used for garbage management and pollution control.

stem: Complete the following flow chart: 'Need of Environmental Conservation' is at the centre, with six boxes around it. Two are given: 'To maintain the balance in nature' and 'To solve the natural and artificial problems'. Fill the remaining four boxes.
solution:
Need of Environmental Conservation:
- To maintain the balance in nature (given).
- To solve the natural and artificial problems (given).
- To conserve biodiversity and protect species of plants and animals from extinction.
- To control the pollution of air, water and soil.
- To use natural resources carefully so that they remain available for future generations.
- To keep the environment healthy for the survival and good health of human beings and other organisms.

stem: Write any three characteristic features of class "Aves".
solution: Characteristic features of class Aves: (1) They are completely adapted for aerial life; the body is spindle-shaped to minimise air resistance during flight. (2) They are warm-blooded (homeotherms), so they keep their body temperature constant. (3) Forelimbs are modified into wings, the exoskeleton is in the form of feathers and the jaws are modified into a beak. Examples: peacock, parrot, pigeon, duck, penguin.

stem: (a) What are vestigial organs? (b) Write two names of some vestigial organs in human body. (c) Write the names of those animals in whom same organs are used? Give two examples.
solution: (a) Degenerated or underdeveloped, useless organs of organisms are called vestigial organs. Such an organ, though non-functional in one organism, may be functional in another, and so it is an evidence of evolution. (b) Vestigial organs in the human body: the appendix and the muscles of the ear pinna (also the tail-bone or coccyx, wisdom teeth and body hair). (c) The appendix is a useful, fully functional organ in ruminant animals, and the muscles of the ear pinna are functional in monkeys, which use them to move the ear pinna.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: How energy is formed from oxidation of carbohydrates, fats and proteins? Correct the diagram given below:
solution:
Carbohydrates (glucose) are oxidised step by step. In glycolysis, in the cytoplasm, glucose is broken into pyruvic acid. Pyruvic acid enters the mitochondria and is converted into acetyl co-enzyme A. Acetyl-CoA is completely oxidised by the Krebs cycle, giving \(CO_2\), \(H_2O\) and energy. When carbohydrates are insufficient, fats (lipids) are converted into fatty acids and proteins into amino acids; both are converted into acetyl-CoA and oxidised by the Krebs cycle to obtain energy.

Corrected diagram (the bottom boxes Proteins and Fats are interchanged, Krebs cycle is not a starting food, and the top of the chart is the final product):
- Carbohydrates \(\rightarrow\) Glycolysis \(\rightarrow\) Pyruvic acid \(\rightarrow\) Acetyl Co-enzyme A
- Fats (lipids) \(\rightarrow\) Fatty acids \(\rightarrow\) Acetyl Co-enzyme A
- Proteins \(\rightarrow\) Amino acids \(\rightarrow\) Acetyl Co-enzyme A
- Acetyl Co-enzyme A \(\rightarrow\) Krebs cycle \(\rightarrow\) \(CO_2 + H_2O\) + Energy
figureNote: Incorrect flow chart to be corrected: bottom row Proteins, Kreb's cycle, Fats; above them Lipid, Glycolysis, Amino acids; then a blank box, Acetyl Co-Enzyme A, a blank box and Pyruvic Acid at the top, p-07

stem: Observe the diagram and answer the following questions: (a) Which type of energy is created in the above diagram? (b) Which type of fuel is used in power plant? (c) State one problem created in such type of power plant.
solution: The diagram shows a thermal power plant. (a) Electrical energy is created. The chemical energy in coal is converted into thermal energy in the boiler, the steam drives the turbine, and the generator connected to the turbine produces electrical energy. (b) Coal, a fossil fuel, is used. (c) Burning coal causes air pollution: gases such as carbon dioxide, sulphur oxides and nitrogen oxides and soot particles are released, which are harmful to health and cause respiratory problems. (The reserves of coal are also limited.)
figureNote: Schematic of a thermal power plant: stack, boiler with fuel and air inputs, turbine, generator, condenser, pumps and cooling tower, p-08

stem: Explain the importance of Biopesticides in organic farming.
solution: Organic farming completely bans chemical fertilizers and pesticides. Chemical pesticides such as DDT and malathion are poisons: they enter the food web through food and water, undergo biomagnification, harm other plants and animals and cause skin diseases in humans. Biopesticides are bacterial and fungal toxins (and some species of fungi and viruses) that destroy pests and pathogens; such toxins can also be built into crop plants by biotechnology, so insects do not feed on them. Spinosad, a by-product of fermentation, is a biopesticide. Biopesticides act on pests without polluting soil and water and without harming humans and useful organisms, so they protect crops while keeping the natural balance. Hence they are important in organic farming.

stem: Complete the following conceptual picture and write its uses in treatment of various diseases: 'Uses of stem cells' is at the centre, with three empty boxes.
solution:
Uses of stem cells:
- Cell therapy: stem cells are used to replace dead cells in conditions like diabetes, myocardial infarction, Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease.
- Production of blood cells: stem cells are used to produce the blood cells required in conditions like anaemia, thalassemia and leukemia.
- Organ transplantation: on failure of organs like the kidney and liver, these organs can be produced with the help of stem cells and transplanted.

stem: Which are three objectives of disaster management?
solution: Objectives of disaster management: (1) Saving human life during the calamity and releasing (rescuing) the people. (2) Supplying essential commodities to the people to reduce the effect of the disaster. (3) Rehabilitating the disaster victims and restoring human life in the region; also taking protective measures so that such a disaster does not recur in future and its intensity is reduced.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Which type of hormones are secreted in female reproductive system?
context: Answer the following questions on the human female reproductive system:
solution: The ovaries secrete the female sex hormones estrogen and progesterone, which control the menstrual cycle and prepare the uterus for pregnancy.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: When does menopause period stop?
context: Answer the following questions on the human female reproductive system:
solution: At the age of about 45 to 50 years, the secretion of hormones controlling the female reproductive system stops or becomes irregular, and the menstrual period stops. This stoppage of functioning of the female reproductive system is called menopause.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: How many ovaries are there in female foetus at the time of birth?
context: Answer the following questions on the human female reproductive system:
solution: A female foetus has a pair of ovaries (two ovaries) at the time of birth, and they contain 2 to 4 million immature oocytes.

stem: Give two examples of: Hobbies to reduce stress.
solution: Hobbies to reduce stress: (1) Reading. (2) Gardening. (Photography, music, drawing and bird watching also help.)

stem: Give two examples of: Diseases endangering the social health.
solution: Diseases endangering the social health: (1) AIDS. (2) T.B. (tuberculosis). Leprosy and mental disorders are further examples.

stem: Give two examples of: Physical problems arising due to excessive use of mobile phones.
solution: Physical problems due to excessive use of mobile phones: (1) Headache. (2) Insomnia (sleeplessness). Tiredness, joint pains and problems in vision also arise.

stem: Give two examples of: Activities under the jurisdiction of cyber crime laws.
solution: Activities under cyber crime laws: (1) Hacking, that is, obtaining confidential information of the government, institutes or companies from the internet and misusing it. (2) Piracy, that is, illegal use or sale of others' software, photos, videos or music obtained from the internet. Opening fake social-media accounts to harass people is another example.

stem: Write problems due to alcoholism.
solution: Problems due to alcoholism: (1) The efficiency of the nervous system (especially the brain) and the liver decreases, and the lifespan of the person is reduced. (2) The addicted person cannot think rationally and faces social, mental and family problems along with physical illness. In adolescents, brain development is hindered, so memory and learning slow down.
